subject: Vector Bridge: Fallback & Rollback runbook for partner pilots
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@pinecone.io>, Maya Singh <maya@vectorops.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vector Bridge: Fallback & Rollback runbook for partner pilots

Alex / Maya —

Thanks for the sync yesterday. As we agreed, before we flip the pilot into production traffic we need a short, actionable fallback and rollback runbook that covers:

- detection signals (error rates, latency spikes, index misses)
- automated fallback routing (pgvector/S3 fallback path + Pinecone read-only)
- safe rollback steps and cutover window expectations
- on-call escalation paths and SLAs (who does what within 30 / 60 / 120 mins)

I've attached a first draft (vec-bridge-fallback-runbook-v1.pdf) and a one-page mutual action plan (pilot-MAP.xlsx) that maps responsibilities across teams. Can you review and call out any gating items from Pinecone or VectorOps by EOD Tuesday so we can lock the canary?

High-level ask: confirm the fastest detectable signal for an index miss in Pinecone (expected metric name and alert threshold) and whether you can enable a read-only replica option for the pilot to reduce write-induced instability during rollback.

Thanks —
Marissa
Sr. Partner GTM, Redwood Inference
redwood.com
[Attachment: vec-bridge-fallback-runbook-v1.pdf (application/pdf)]
[Attachment: pilot-MAP.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@pinecone.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Maya Singh <maya@vectorops.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vector Bridge: Fallback & Rollback runbook for partner pilots

Marissa —

Appreciate the draft. Quick answers up front:

- Detection signal: our recommended metric is pod.index.errors_per_min (Prometheus) and a rolling 5-min rate > 0.5% of requests should be treated as a safety margin. We can expose that via the pilot metrics endpoint (we'll provide exact PromQL).
- Read-only replica: we can spin a read-replica for the pilot environment but it requires a short maintenance window (~15 minutes) to snapshot and warm the replica.

Feedback on the runbook: add an explicit step to switch client routing to the read-replica (or to Redwood's pgvector fallback) and to incrementally reduce write QPS by 25% buckets during the rollback window. Also include a short checklist for cache invalidation (KV cache + prefix caches) — failure there is a common root cause.

We'll have a detailed PromQL snippet and the replica prep checklist by Monday morning PST.

- Alex
Head of Integrations, Pinecone

Looping Sergio for ops input — Sergio, can you confirm we can implement the 25% write-QPS ramp-down and whether that requires a routing policy change in Redwood Dedicated? Also planning to add the on-call rotation for this pilot into our shared calendar.

Vanessa
Partner Ops

From: Maya Singh <maya@vectorops.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@pinecone.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vector Bridge: Fallback & Rollback runbook for partner pilots

On Mon, Oct 18, 2027 at 08:12 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex / Maya —
>
> Thanks for the sync yesterday. As we agreed, before we flip the pilot into production traffic we need a short, actionable fallback and rollback runbook that covers...

Thanks Marissa — this looks good. VectorOps will:

- Validate the Pinecone PromQL snippet against our test harness and report back with alert thresholds by COB Tuesday.
- Provide a small script to perform the snapshot-and-warm for our connector (we can automate the 15-minute window).
- Sign off on the MAP responsibilities where VectorOps is owner for connector lifecycle and Pinecone owns replica readiness.

One open question from our infra lead: can Redwood provide a short-lived API key with read-only scope that rotates every 24 hours for the warm replica step? If yes, we can avoid sharing long-lived credentials in the pilot.

We'll also add an explicit rollback dry-run into our acceptance checklist and propose a one-hour canary window (first 15 minutes slow ramp, next 30 minutes under watch, final 15 minutes decision point).

Cheers,
Maya Singh
VP, Solutions — VectorOps Consulting

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vector Bridge: Fallback & Rollback runbook for partner pilots

All —

Quick ops confirmation after internal run-through:

- We can implement the 25% QPS ramp-down via routing policy flags in Redwood Dedicated; no infra changes required. I will add the routing toggle to the pilot runbook and document the exact command set.
- We can provide a 24-hour rotating short-lived read-only API key for the replica warm step. Security will issue the rotation and we will provision an automated key minting job.
- On-call: Laura will be primary (Vector partner coordination), Vanessa secondary (Redwood partner ops), and Sergio tertiary for infra escalations. I'll add the rotation to the shared calendar and update the MAP.

Next steps:
- Marissa: tuck Alex's PromQL and VectorOps' snapshot script into the runbook and we'll schedule a dry-run on Oct 25.
- Vanessa: update the pilot-MAP assignment matrix and share final doc.

Sergio
Sr. Infra Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
